artworkProvenance.prompt: COMBEDSLIP FENCEROW for Glaze. One separate original square pure artwork of a whole recognizable North American fencerow specimen in hand-shaped fired earthenware, isolated on genuine transparent alpha. The dominant tactile effect is deliberately broad WET COMBED SLIPWARE. A near-black coffee-colored liquid clay ground and several pale golden cream slip trails are run across the broad continuous convex surface. While both are wet the actual comb is dragged perpendicularly through THE SAME CONTINUOUS PARALLEL TRAILS, giving each trail matching repeated stretched curves, alternating inward and outward. Four to six clearly visible thick honey-and-black slip trails, bending in two or three aligned feather passages across each large field, with substantial dark negative intervals. Each line flows uninterrupted between turns. Keep the strokes broad enough to read at 85 pixels. The material looks like a hand-formed, low rounded, compact clay sculpture or steep low relief with a quiet exposed dark ochre wall on one edge. A thin patient satin-fired glaze catches soft raking light with a restrained single broad highlight. Very modest pinholes and rough pores around the exposed raw clay edge. Main form entirely made of clay. Clay is physically thick below a very thin surface skin. One defined face of visible decoration, clear broad quiet sections and true anatomical silhouette. Avoid whole-face plain terracotta, hairline smoke and soot, incised white grooves, cracked stone, independent hairline marbling, geological banded stone, metallic foil, loose feathers or feather-shaped components, herringbone textile, wood grain, dots everywhere, exaggerated chrome gloss, polymer shine, busy botanical pattern outside the specimen, cartoon eyes. No edge frame, saucer, rectangle, plaque, ceramic tile backing, dipped display pedestal, environment, corner art, cast ground shadow, logo, signature, UI or writing. Preserve all body appendages on a balanced form, with a comfortable transparent border on every side. FIRST SUBJECT: One entire identifiable CEDAR WAXWING in left profile on a short attached dry fence-row twig of the same earthenware. Lean long smooth fawn body, triangular swept crest, compact beak, distinct continuous black eye mask bounded by a fine cream stripe, one dark small eye, one partly visible folded wing, straight tapered tail with full pale yellow terminal bar, and exactly two petite believable feet gripping the twig. The broad folded wing and upper flank are ONE substantial satin slip field with near-black and honey contrasting medium-width parallel trails and three distinct aligned feather bends through those same trails. Make the body broad enough to read the repeated combed flow within the wing. The unpatterned cream head and buff breast preserve waxwing anatomy and the clean black mask reads first. Protect the shape of the central short crest peak, beak, twig ends, toes and yellow lower tail end. All comfortably inside the border. A faint red earthen slip tip on the wing can be one tiny restrained accent. No graphic decorative swirls or carved linework. No round medallion, branch extending beyond the two feet, berries in the beak or printed clay extras.
